description:
Given a seed that fails, find the smallest fault schedule that still reproduces it.

Replay the run with faults progressively removed -- delta-debugging over the fault journal -- and keep the smallest schedule that still trips an oracle. This is what converts 'chaos found something' into a three-line repro that can be attached to a ticket and fixed.

Requires the schedule to be fully deterministic given a seed, and requires replay to be reliable enough that a non-reproducing run means 'this fault was not necessary' rather than 'we got lucky'. Flaky replay makes shrinking actively misleading, so this child depends on replay-by-seed being trustworthy first.

Output: a minimized fault schedule plus the oracle violation it produces, in a form that can be pasted into a bug ticket.
title: Shrink failing runs to a minimal fault schedule
